## 8H4

```{r}
library(rethinking)
library(tidyverse)
library(brms)
data(nettle)

# estimate language per pop
nettle <- nettle |> 
  mutate(lang.per.cap = num.lang/k.pop)
```

Our outcomes are on very different scales, so we'll center everything. We can use the vague $Normal(0,1)$ prior on the z scale. I'll use a wider prior on the intercept, and exponential prior on sigma.

I'll estimate the models for A, B, and C in the same code chunk.

```{r}
priors <- c(set_prior("normal(0,1)", class = "b"),
            set_prior("normal(0,2)", class = "Intercept"),
            set_prior("exponential(1)", class = "sigma"))

mA <- brm(scale(log(lang.per.cap)) ~ 
            scale(log(area)) + scale(mean.growing.season), 
          data = nettle,
          prior = priors)

mB <- brm(scale(log(lang.per.cap)) ~ 
            scale(log(area)) + scale(sd.growing.season), 
          data = nettle,
          prior = priors)

mC <- brm(scale(log(lang.per.cap)) ~ 
            scale(log(area)) + 
            scale(sd.growing.season)*scale(mean.growing.season), 
          data = nettle,
          prior = priors)
```

I'll suggest that area interacts with the variance of the growing season
more uncertain growing season + smaller areas = higher linguistic diversity
as the working hypothesis.
